- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 7–14 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model underestimates; increase forecast by 15–30% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >1.5x), model often overcorrects; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 20–40% for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 2.0), model tends to hold too high; apply downward bias of 0.1–0.3 per day until reversion.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; weight sentiment history 30% more in final forecast adjustment.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67…), model tends to oscillate; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average before final output.
